fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled RLE packet header byte read from the truncated input file; the high bit (c & 0x80) selects the RLE-pixel branch and count=(c&0x7f)+1 sets the run length.

Root cause: the return value of readRawData is not checked. The stream ends before pixel_size bytes are available, so zero bytes are read and the stack buffer pixel[8] keeps uninitialized stack contents instead of being zeroed (unlike the palette/non-RLE paths which check dataRead and memset the tail).
The uninitialized byte of pixel is copied verbatim into the malloc'd image buffer, propagating the uninitialized value into the decoded image.
For the paletted (RLE-indexed) image type, the palette index byte idx is loaded from the image buffer, which received the uninitialized byte from the truncated RLE pixel.

fine_trace.code: scanline[x] = qRgb(palette[3 * idx + 2], palette[3 * idx + 1], palette[3 * idx + 0]);
fine_trace.note: Sink: the uninitialized idx is used to compute the palette array index 3*idx+k, i.e. uninitialized memory is used as an address for memory loads from palette (MSan use-of-uninitialized-value on the palette[3*idx+2] access).

relation.right: image buffer byte copied from uninitialized pixel

vuln_logic.issue_alignment: Truncated RLE-indexed TGA input: the packet header claims an RLE run, but the stream ends before pixel_size bytes of pixel data are present, so readRawData returns fewer bytes and the unchecked remainder of the stack pixel buffer is copied into the image. The entire pixel_size worth of 'pixel' therefore does not always contain valid data (either read from the file or explicitly set to 0), and the uninitialized palette index is later used to address the palette array, i.e. uninitialized memory is read in the pixel structure.
